source.text: Ἀδελφοί, ἐὰν καὶ προλημφθῇ ἄνθρωπος ἔν τινι παραπτώματι, ὑμεῖς οἱ πνευματικοὶ καταρτίζετε τὸν τοιοῦτον ἐν πνεύματι πραΰτητος, σκοπῶν σεαυτόν, μὴ καὶ σὺ πειρασθῇς.

records.literal_gloss: Brothers, if even is overtaken a man in some trespass, you the spiritual [ones] restore the such [one] in a spirit of gentleness, watching yourself, lest also you be tempted.

en.L: {{gender:Brothers and sisters|Brothers}}, if someone is even caught in some wrongdoing, you who are spiritual, restore such a one in a spirit of gentleness, keeping watch on yourself, so that you also are not tempted.
en.B: {{gender:Brothers and sisters|Brothers}}, suppose someone is caught out in some wrongdoing. You who are spiritual must set that person right again, and do it with a gentle spirit. Keep an eye on yourself as you do, in case you are tempted too.
en.R: {{gender:Brothers and sisters|Brothers}}, someone among you may be found doing something wrong. If that happens, you whose lives are guided by the Spirit should help that person back onto the right path. Be gentle about it. And watch out for yourself, so that you are not tempted as well.

es.L: Hermanos, si incluso alguien es sorprendido en alguna transgresión, {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, los espirituales, {{plural_you:restauren|restaurad}} a tal persona en un espíritu de mansedumbre, mirándote a ti mismo, para que no seas tentado también tú.
es.B: Hermanos, supongamos que alguien es sorprendido en alguna transgresión. {{plural_you:Ustedes|Vosotros}}, los que {{plural_you:son|sois}} espirituales, {{plural_you:deben|debéis}} restaurar a esa persona, y {{plural_you:háganlo|hacedlo}} con espíritu apacible. Y tú, mientras lo haces, vigílate a ti mismo, no vaya a ser que también tú seas tentado.
es.R: Hermanos, puede ser que alguno de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} sea descubierto haciendo algo malo. Si eso pasa, {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, los que {{plural_you:se dejan|os dejáis}} guiar por el Espíritu, {{plural_you:deben|debéis}} ayudar a esa persona a volver al buen camino. {{plural_you:Háganlo|Hacedlo}} con amabilidad. Y cada uno tenga cuidado consigo mismo, para no ser tentado también.

sw.L: Ndugu, hata mtu akikamatwa katika kosa fulani, ninyi watu wa kiroho, mrejesheni mtu wa namna hiyo kwa roho ya upole, ukijitazama mwenyewe, ili nawe usijaribiwe.
sw.B: Ndugu, tuseme mtu amekamatwa akifanya kosa fulani. Ninyi mlio wa kiroho mnapaswa kumrudisha mtu huyo katika hali njema, kwa roho ya upole. Nawe, unapofanya hivyo, jichunge mwenyewe, ili usijaribiwe pia.
sw.R: Ndugu, huenda mtu miongoni mwenu akagunduliwa anafanya jambo baya. Hilo likitokea, ninyi mnaoongozwa na Roho mnapaswa kumsaidia mtu huyo arudi kwenye njia sahihi. Fanyeni hivyo kwa upole. Na kila mmoja ajichunge mwenyewe, ili naye asijaribiwe.

fr.L: {{gender:Frères et sœurs|Frères}}, si même quelqu’un est surpris en quelque faute, vous, les spirituels, relevez celui-là dans un esprit de douceur, veillant sur toi-même, de peur que toi aussi tu ne sois tenté.
fr.B: {{gender:Frères et sœurs|Frères}}, supposons que quelqu’un soit pris en faute. Vous qui êtes spirituels, relevez-le, et faites-le avec un esprit de douceur. Et toi, fais attention à toi-même, pour ne pas être tenté à ton tour.
fr.R: {{gender:Frères et sœurs|Frères}}, il peut arriver que quelqu’un parmi vous soit surpris en train de faire quelque chose de mal. Si cela arrive, vous dont la vie est guidée par l’Esprit, aidez cette personne à retrouver le bon chemin. Faites-le avec douceur. Et que chacun fasse attention à lui-même, pour ne pas être tenté lui aussi.

ko.L: {{gender:형제자매|형제}} 여러분, 어떤 사람이 무슨 잘못에 빠진 것이 드러나더라도, 영적인 사람인 여러분은 온유한 마음으로 그런 사람을 바로잡아 주십시오. 당신 자신도 살펴서, 당신도 시험에 빠지지 않도록 하십시오.
ko.B: {{gender:형제자매|형제}} 여러분, 누군가 어떤 잘못을 저지르다가 드러났다고 합시다. 영적인 사람인 여러분은 그 사람을 다시 바로 세워 주어야 합니다. 온유한 마음으로 그렇게 하십시오. 그러면서 당신 자신도 살펴서, 당신도 시험에 빠지지 않도록 하십시오.
ko.R: {{gender:형제자매|형제}} 여러분, 여러분 가운데 누군가 잘못을 저지르다가 들킬 수도 있습니다. 그런 일이 생기면, 성령의 이끄심을 따라 사는 여러분이 그 사람을 도와서 바른길로 돌아오게 해 주십시오. 부드럽게 하십시오. 그리고 당신 자신도 조심하십시오. 당신도 유혹에 넘어가지 않도록 하십시오.

vi.L: Thưa {{gender:anh chị em|anh em}}, nếu có ai bị bắt gặp đang phạm một lỗi lầm nào đó, thì anh chị em là những người thuộc linh hãy lấy tinh thần hiền hòa mà sửa lại người ấy, và hãy coi chừng chính mình, kẻo chính mình cũng bị cám dỗ.
vi.B: Thưa {{gender:anh chị em|anh em}}, giả sử có ai bị phát hiện đang phạm một lỗi lầm nào đó. Anh chị em là những người thuộc linh phải giúp người ấy đứng lại cho ngay thẳng, và làm điều đó với tinh thần hiền hòa. Đồng thời hãy giữ mình, kẻo chính mình cũng bị cám dỗ.
vi.R: Thưa {{gender:anh chị em|anh em}}, có thể có người trong anh chị em bị thấy đang làm điều sai trái. Nếu điều đó xảy ra, anh chị em là những người có đời sống được Thánh Linh dẫn dắt, hãy giúp người ấy trở lại con đường đúng. Hãy làm điều đó cách nhẹ nhàng. Và hãy coi chừng chính mình, để mình cũng không bị cám dỗ.

decisions.choice: caught: taken by surprise in the act, found out
alternatives: overtaken: carried away by a sin before the person can resist
decisions.reason: προλαμβάνω means to take or seize beforehand, and with καὶ ("even") the clause most naturally pictures someone surprised or found out in the act. The other sense, being overtaken by sin before one sees it coming, is also possible. Either way the person has really done wrong, and the point is how the church responds.

decisions.choice: the spiritual: those who live by the Spirit, as 5:16-25 has described
alternatives: a spiritual elite within the church
said with irony, of those who think themselves spiritual
decisions.reason: πνευματικοὶ picks up the Spirit language of 5:16-25: walking by the Spirit, led by the Spirit, bearing the Spirit's fruit. Paul is addressing every believer who lives that way, not a special class. Some hear a touch of irony aimed at people who prided themselves on being spiritual, but nothing in the sentence requires it.

decisions.choice: restore: set right, mend what is broken
decisions.reason: καταρτίζω is used of mending nets (Mark 1:19) and of putting things into proper order. The aim is to bring the person back, not to punish.

decisions.choice: a spirit of gentleness: a gentle attitude, the gentleness the Spirit produces
alternatives: the Holy Spirit, who gives gentleness
decisions.reason: πνεύματι here most naturally means a person's attitude, as in 1 Corinthians 4:21. Gentleness, πραΰτης, is one of the fruit of the Spirit in 5:23, so the Spirit stands behind the attitude even if the word does not name him directly.

decisions.choice: Paul turns from "you" plural to "you" singular: each helper must watch himself or herself
alternatives: the singular is only a change of style
decisions.reason: After the plural command, σκοπῶν σεαυτόν and σὺ are singular. Paul presses the warning on each person individually: anyone who helps another out of a fault can fall into the same or another temptation.

decisions.choice: {{gender:Brothers and sisters|Brothers}}
decisions.reason: Paul is writing to all the believers in Galatia, women and men (3:28). Traditional is one tap away.

decisions.choice: wrongdoing (B); doing something wrong (R)
decisions.reason: "Trespass" now mostly means entering private land; plain words say what the Greek word means, a false step, a wrong act.

decisions.choice: you whose lives are guided by the Spirit
decisions.reason: Readable says what "spiritual" means here (m2), using the language of 5:16-18.

decisions.choice: ustedes / vosotros forms
decisions.reason: As in the rest of Galatians, every plural "you" and its verb is a reader setting: ustedes (Latin America, the default) or vosotros (Spain).

decisions.choice: hermanos, no setting
decisions.reason: As in Romans 1:13, "hermanos" already covers brothers and sisters, so there is no gender span. The same holds for the generic "alguien", "cada uno" and "una persona" later in the chapter, where the English Literal has gender spans.

decisions.choice: tú (L, B); cada uno (R)
decisions.reason: The Greek turns to the singular (m5), and Spanish can follow with "tú", which needs no setting because it is the same in Latin America and Spain. Readable says "cada uno" so that the sudden switch does not confuse a young reader.

decisions.choice: ndugu, no setting
decisions.reason: "Ndugu" already means brothers and sisters, and Swahili pronouns and verb prefixes do not mark gender, so the Swahili text of this chapter has no gender spans.

decisions.choice: toi-même, toi aussi (L, B), singular after the plural "vous"
decisions.reason: Paul turns from the plural to the singular to press the warning on each helper (m5). French can show the change, so Literal and Balanced keep it; Readable says "que chacun".

decisions.choice: quelqu'un ... celui-là, with no gender setting
decisions.reason: The Greek word means any human being. French says "quelqu'un", already inclusive, and refers back to it with the generic "celui-là", as the French style guide sets out.

decisions.choice: "여러분" for the plural "you" and "당신" for the singular
decisions.reason: Paul turns from the plural to the singular, so that each helper watches himself or herself (the meaning decision). Korean marks the turn with "당신", as at 4:7.

decisions.choice: "어떤 사람", "그 사람", "자기" with no gender spans, here and through the chapter
alternatives: gender spans where the English Literal has them (6:3, 6:4, 6:7, 6:8)
decisions.reason: The English Literal offers "they" or "he" for a general person. Korean says "사람" and "자기", which already mean a person of either sex, and rarely uses a pronoun at all, so the gender setting has nothing to change.

decisions.choice: "những người thuộc linh" (L, B); "những người có đời sống được Thánh Linh dẫn dắt" (R)
decisions.reason: The spiritual are those who live by the Spirit (m2). "Thuộc linh" (of the Spirit) is the word of the Vietnamese Romans (1:11; 7:14); "thiêng liêng" would mean only sacred.

decisions.choice: "chính mình" for the singular "you" in "watching yourself"
decisions.reason: Paul turns to each helper in the singular (m5). Vietnamese can say it with the reflexive "chính mình", which is singular in sense and needs no pronoun of address, so the sentence does not change from "anh chị em" to "bạn" halfway through.

source.text: ἀλλήλων τὰ βάρη βαστάζετε, καὶ οὕτως ἀναπληρώσετε τὸν νόμον τοῦ Χριστοῦ.

records.literal_gloss: Of one another the burdens bear, and thus you will fulfill the law of the Christ.

en.L: Bear the burdens of one another, and in this way you will fulfill the law of the {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}.
en.B: Take up one another's heavy loads, and so you will fulfill the law of {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}.
en.R: Help each other carry the things that weigh you down. When you do, you will be doing all that the law of {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} asks.

es.L: {{plural_you:Carguen|Cargad}} con los pesos los unos de los otros, y de este modo {{plural_you:cumplirán|cumpliréis}} la ley del {{christos:Cristo|Mesías}}.
es.B: {{plural_you:Compartan|Compartid}} unos con otros el peso de las cargas pesadas, y así {{plural_you:darán|daréis}} pleno cumplimiento a la ley {{christos:de Cristo|del Mesías}}.
es.R: {{plural_you:Ayúdense|Ayudaos}} entre {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} a cargar con lo que {{plural_you:les|os}} pesa. Cuando lo {{plural_you:hacen|hacéis}}, {{plural_you:están|estáis}} cumpliendo todo lo que pide la ley {{christos:de Cristo|del Mesías}}.

sw.L: Bebeaneni mizigo, na hivyo mtaitimiza sheria ya {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}}.
sw.B: Saidianeni kubeba mizigo mizito, na kwa kufanya hivyo mtaitimiza sheria ya {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}}.
sw.R: Saidianeni kubeba mambo yanayowalemea. Mkifanya hivyo, mtakuwa mnatenda yote ambayo sheria ya {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}} inadai.

fr.L: Portez les fardeaux les uns des autres, et ainsi vous accomplirez la loi du {{christos:Christ|Messie}}.
fr.B: Portez les fardeaux les uns des autres, et vous accomplirez ainsi la loi du {{christos:Christ|Messie}}.
fr.R: Aidez-vous les uns les autres à porter ce qui vous pèse. Si vous le faites, vous ferez tout ce que demande la loi du {{christos:Christ|Messie}}.

ko.L: 서로의 짐을 지십시오. 그렇게 하여 {{christos:그리스도|메시아}}의 법을 이루게 될 것입니다.
ko.B: 서로의 무거운 짐을 져 주십시오. 그러면 여러분은 {{christos:그리스도|메시아}}의 법을 이루게 될 것입니다.
ko.R: 서로를 짓누르는 무거운 짐을 함께 져 주십시오. 그렇게 하면 여러분은 {{christos:그리스도|메시아}}의 법이 요구하는 모든 것을 행하는 것입니다.

vi.L: Hãy mang gánh nặng cho nhau, và như vậy anh chị em sẽ làm trọn luật pháp của {{christos:Đấng Christ|Đấng Mê-si-a}}.
vi.B: Hãy gánh lấy những gánh nặng của nhau, và như vậy anh chị em sẽ làm trọn luật pháp của {{christos:Đấng Christ|Đấng Mê-si-a}}.
vi.R: Hãy giúp nhau mang những gì đang đè nặng trên nhau. Khi làm như vậy, anh chị em đang làm trọn mọi điều mà luật pháp của {{christos:Đấng Christ|Đấng Mê-si-a}} đòi hỏi.

decisions.choice: burdens: heavy loads, anything too heavy for a person to carry alone
alternatives: only the moral failures of verse 1
decisions.reason: βάρη are weights that press a person down. Coming just after verse 1, they include the weight of sin and temptation, but the word is general and covers any hardship a fellow believer is struggling under.

decisions.choice: the law of Christ: the command to love, as Christ taught and lived it
alternatives: a new code of rules given by Christ
the law of Moses as Christ interprets it
decisions.reason: Paul has just said that the whole law is fulfilled in one word, "love your neighbor as yourself" (5:14), and has described Christ as the one who loved him and gave himself for him (2:20). Bearing others' burdens is that love put into practice. The phrase is pointed in a letter where the opponents urge the Galatians to take on the law of Moses: the law believers live by is Christ's. Paul uses a similar phrase in 1 Corinthians 9:21.

decisions.choice: follow SBLGNT: "you will fulfill", a future
decisions.reason: Many manuscripts read a command, "and so fulfill the law of Christ"; the two forms differ by a single letter. SBLGNT reads the future ἀναπληρώσετε, a promise of what carrying burdens achieves. The sense is close either way. Reviewers should check the apparatus.

decisions.choice: {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} (L); {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} (B, R)
decisions.reason: Title setting. Literal keeps the article.

decisions.choice: you will be doing all that the law of Christ asks
alternatives: you will fulfill the law of Christ
decisions.reason: Readable says plainly what "fulfill" means: to do in full what the law requires.

decisions.choice: los pesos
decisions.reason: Literal says "pesos" (weights) for βάρη, so that it stays distinct from "carga", used for the different word φορτίον in verse 5 (m3 there).

decisions.choice: {{christos:Cristo|Mesías}} after "del" (L); {{christos:de Cristo|del Mesías}} (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Greek article, "la ley del Cristo" or "del Mesías", here and in verse 12; Balanced and Readable use the usual Spanish "de Cristo", and the span takes in the preposition.

decisions.choice: bebeaneni
alternatives: bebeni mizigo ya ninyi kwa ninyi
decisions.reason: Swahili has a reciprocal verb form, "kubebeana" (to carry for one another), which says "bear one another's burdens" in one word without a clumsy possessive.

decisions.choice: les fardeaux (6:2); la charge (6:5); la loi du Christ, lowercase
decisions.reason: Paul uses two different words in verses 2 and 5 (m3 on 6:4), and French keeps them apart. The law of Christ is the command to love as Christ taught it (m2), not the law of Moses, so it has no capital.

decisions.choice: "{{christos:그리스도|메시아}}의 법" at every level
decisions.reason: The law of Christ is the command to love as Christ taught and lived it (the meaning decision), not the law of Moses, so Korean says "법" (law, rule) rather than "율법", as Romans 3:27 and 8:2 do for a law in a wider sense.

decisions.choice: "luật pháp của {{christos:Đấng Christ|Đấng Mê-si-a}}"
decisions.reason: The law of Christ is the command to love as Christ taught and lived it (m2). Vietnamese keeps "luật pháp", the word used for the law of Moses through the letter, so the reader hears Paul's turn: the burden-bearing of love fulfills a law, as in 5:14.

source.text: εἰ γὰρ δοκεῖ τις εἶναί τι μηδὲν ὤν, φρεναπατᾷ ἑαυτόν·

records.literal_gloss: For if thinks anyone to be something, nothing being, he deceives himself;

en.L: For if anyone thinks [{{gender:themselves|himself}}] to be something while being nothing, {{gender:they deceive themselves|he deceives himself}}.
en.B: For those who think they are something when they are nothing are only fooling themselves.
en.R: People who think they are too important to help others are fooling themselves. In fact they are nothing.

es.L: Porque si alguien piensa que es algo mientras no es nada, se engaña a sí mismo.
es.B: Los que piensan que son algo cuando no son nada solo se están engañando a sí mismos.
es.R: Quienes se creen demasiado importantes para ayudar a otros se engañan a sí mismos. En realidad no son nada.

sw.L: Kwa maana kama mtu yeyote anadhani kuwa yeye ni kitu, ilhali si kitu, anajidanganya.
sw.B: Watu wanaodhani kuwa wao ni kitu fulani, ilhali si kitu, wanajidanganya tu.
sw.R: Watu wanaojiona kuwa wa maana sana kiasi cha kutowasaidia wengine wanajidanganya. Kwa kweli wao si kitu.

fr.L: Car si quelqu’un pense être quelque chose, alors qu’il n’est rien, il se trompe lui-même.
fr.B: Car celui qui se croit quelque chose alors qu’il n’est rien ne fait que se tromper lui-même.
fr.R: Ceux qui se croient trop importants pour aider les autres se trompent eux-mêmes. En réalité, ils ne sont rien.

ko.L: 누구든지 아무것도 아니면서 무엇이라도 되는 줄로 생각하면, 자기를 속이는 것입니다.
ko.B: 아무것도 아니면서 자기가 대단한 사람이라고 생각하는 사람은 자기 자신을 속이는 것일 뿐입니다.
ko.R: 자기는 너무 중요한 사람이라서 다른 사람을 도울 필요가 없다고 생각하는 사람은 자기 자신을 속이는 것입니다. 사실 그는 아무것도 아닙니다.

vi.L: Vì nếu có ai nghĩ mình là quan trọng trong khi mình chẳng là gì, người ấy tự lừa dối mình.
vi.B: Vì những ai nghĩ mình là quan trọng trong khi chẳng là gì cả, thì chỉ tự lừa dối mình mà thôi.
vi.R: Những ai nghĩ rằng mình quá quan trọng để giúp đỡ người khác là đang tự lừa dối mình. Thật ra họ chẳng là gì cả.

decisions.choice: for: the reason why some will not bear others' burdens
decisions.reason: γὰρ ties the verse to verses 1-2. Pride, thinking oneself above a fallen brother or sister, is what keeps a person from stooping to help, and it is the danger verse 1 warns of.

decisions.choice: while being nothing: no one has standing of their own before God
alternatives: only those who are proud are nothing
decisions.reason: μηδὲν ὤν could describe the proud person in particular, but Paul's point is wider: no one is "something" in himself or herself (compare 2:6; 1 Corinthians 3:7). To think otherwise is to deceive oneself.

decisions.choice: {{gender:they deceive themselves|he deceives himself}} (L); plural "those", "people" (B, R)
decisions.reason: "Anyone" includes women and men. Literal keeps the singular with the gender setting; Balanced and Readable make the sentence plural so that no pronoun is needed.

decisions.choice: think they are too important to help others
decisions.reason: Readable makes the link with verses 1-2 explicit (m1).

decisions.choice: quelqu'un ... il ... lui-même, with no gender setting (L, and in 6:4 "chacun ... il")
alternatives: gender spans on the pronouns, as in the English Literal
decisions.reason: The English Literal needs {{gender:they|he}} for "anyone". In French "quelqu'un" and "chacun" are generic, and the "il" and "lui-même" that refer back to them are ordinary generic French, so no setting is needed, as the French style guide sets out.

decisions.choice: "ai", "người ấy", "mình", with no gender span (also 6:4-8)
alternatives: a gender span as in the English
decisions.reason: Vietnamese "ai", "người ấy" and the reflexive "mình" do not mark sex, so the English setting has nothing to change in these verses.

source.text: τὸ δὲ ἔργον ἑαυτοῦ δοκιμαζέτω ἕκαστος, καὶ τότε εἰς ἑαυτὸν μόνον τὸ καύχημα ἕξει καὶ οὐκ εἰς τὸν ἕτερον, ἕκαστος γὰρ τὸ ἴδιον φορτίον βαστάσει.

records.literal_gloss: But the work of himself let test each [one], and then as to himself alone the boast he will have and not as to the other; \v 5 for each the own load will carry.

en.L: But let each one test {{gender:their|his}} own work, and then {{gender:they|he}} will have [a ground for] boasting with regard to {{gender:themselves|himself}} alone, and not with regard to the other [person]; \v 5 for each one will carry {{gender:their|his}} own load.
en.B: Each of you should examine your own conduct. Then any pride you take will be in what you yourself have done, not in how you compare with someone else. \v 5 For each of you will have your own load to carry.
en.R: Each of you should look carefully at what you yourself are doing. Then if you have something to be proud of, it will be your own work, and not that you look better than someone else. \v 5 Each of you will have your own load to carry.

es.L: Pero que cada uno ponga a prueba su propia obra, y entonces tendrá [razón para] gloriarse solo en cuanto a sí mismo, y no en cuanto al otro; \v 5 porque cada uno llevará la carga que le es propia.
es.B: Que cada uno ponga a prueba lo que hace. Entonces, si tiene algo de qué sentirse orgulloso, será por su propio trabajo y no por compararse con los demás. \v 5 Porque cada uno tendrá su propia carga que llevar.
es.R: Cada uno debe mirar con cuidado su propia manera de actuar. Así, si tiene algo de lo que sentirse orgulloso, será de su propio trabajo, y no de parecer mejor que otro. \v 5 Cada uno tendrá que llevar su propia carga.

sw.L: Lakini kila mmoja na aichunguze kazi yake binafsi, na ndipo atakuwa na [sababu ya] kujisifu kwa habari yake mwenyewe tu, wala si kwa habari ya mwingine; \v 5 kwa kuwa kila mmoja atabeba mzigo wake binafsi.
sw.B: Kila mmoja wenu achunguze mwenendo wake. Ndipo fahari yoyote atakayokuwa nayo itakuwa juu ya yale aliyoyafanya yeye mwenyewe, wala si kwa kujilinganisha na mwingine. \v 5 Kwa maana kila mmoja wenu atakuwa na mzigo wake wa kubeba.
sw.R: Kila mmoja wenu aangalie kwa makini anachokifanya. Hapo, kama ana kitu cha kujivunia, kitakuwa kazi yake mwenyewe, wala si kwamba anaonekana bora kuliko mwingine. \v 5 Kila mmoja wenu atabeba mzigo wake.

fr.L: Mais que chacun examine sa propre œuvre, et alors il aura de quoi se glorifier par rapport à lui-même seulement, et non par rapport à l’autre ; \v 5 car chacun portera sa propre charge.
fr.B: Que chacun examine sa propre conduite. Alors, s’il trouve de quoi se glorifier, ce sera dans ce qu’il a fait lui-même, et non en se comparant à un autre. \v 5 Car chacun aura sa propre charge à porter.
fr.R: Que chacun regarde attentivement ce qu’il fait lui-même. Alors, s’il a quelque chose dont il peut être fier, ce sera son propre travail, et pas le fait de paraître meilleur qu’un autre. \v 5 Chacun aura sa propre charge à porter.

ko.L: 각 사람은 자기 일을 살펴보십시오. 그러면 자기에게만 자랑할 것이 있고, 다른 사람에게는 [자랑할 것이] 없을 것입니다. \v 5 각 사람이 자기 짐을 질 것이기 때문입니다.
ko.B: 각자 자기가 하는 일을 살펴보십시오. 그러면 자랑할 것이 있더라도, 그것은 자기가 한 일에 있지, 남과 비교하는 데 있지 않을 것입니다. \v 5 각자 자기가 져야 할 짐이 있기 때문입니다.
ko.R: 여러분은 각자 자기가 하는 일을 잘 살펴보십시오. 그러면 자랑할 것이 있다 해도, 그것은 여러분 자신이 한 일일 것입니다. 남보다 나아 보이는 것을 자랑하지는 않을 것입니다. \v 5 각자 자기가 져야 할 짐이 있습니다.

vi.L: Nhưng mỗi người hãy thử nghiệm việc làm của chính mình, và khi đó người ấy sẽ có [lý do để] khoe mình về chính mình mà thôi, chứ không phải so với người khác; \v 5 vì mỗi người sẽ mang gánh của riêng mình.
vi.B: Mỗi người hãy xem xét việc làm của chính mình. Khi đó, nếu có điều gì để tự hào, thì người ấy tự hào về những gì chính mình đã làm, chứ không phải vì so sánh mình với người khác. \v 5 Vì mỗi người sẽ có gánh riêng của mình phải mang.
vi.R: Mỗi người hãy xem xét cẩn thận những gì chính mình đang làm. Rồi nếu có điều gì đáng để tự hào, thì đó sẽ là việc làm của chính mình, chứ không phải vì mình trông khá hơn người khác. \v 5 Mỗi người sẽ có phần gánh riêng của mình phải mang.

decisions.choice: test: examine one's own work to see whether it is genuine
decisions.reason: δοκιμάζω is used for testing metal to prove it is genuine. Instead of measuring others, each person is to examine his or her own conduct (ἔργον, "work", meaning the whole of what one does).

decisions.choice: a person's boast is to rest on his or her own work, not on comparison with someone else
alternatives: boasting is kept private, to oneself
decisions.reason: The two phrases with εἰς set out what the boast is measured against: oneself alone, not the other person. Paul is not encouraging pride; he rules out the kind of pride that comes from feeling superior to someone who has fallen (verses 1-3). The same word for boasting returns in verses 13-14, where Paul's only boast is the cross.

decisions.choice: load: the burden of responsibility that belongs to each person
alternatives: the same thing as the burdens of verse 2
decisions.reason: φορτίον is a different word from βάρη in verse 2. There is no contradiction: believers help one another with burdens too heavy to carry alone, while each remains answerable for his or her own life. Jesus uses the same word for a load in Matthew 11:30.

decisions.choice: will carry: likely looking ahead to God's judgment
alternatives: a general truth about life now
decisions.reason: The future βαστάσει may simply state a rule, but with "reap" in verses 7-9 it most likely looks forward to the day when each person gives account to God (Romans 14:12). The text does not decide between the two.

decisions.choice: each of you ... your own
alternatives: let each one test his own work
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable address the reader directly, which keeps the sense of "each" without a third-person pronoun.

decisions.choice: pride you take (B); something to be proud of (R)
decisions.reason: In current English "boast" is always bad, but here the boast that rests on one's own tested work is not condemned (m2). Literal keeps "boasting".

decisions.choice: {{gender:their|his}} own, {{gender:themselves|himself}}
decisions.reason: Each person is meant, women and men; Literal keeps the singular with the gender setting.

decisions.choice: cada uno ... su (third person)
decisions.reason: The English Balanced and Readable turn to "each of you" to avoid a gendered pronoun. Spanish "su" is not gendered, so it can keep the Greek third person "cada uno", and no plural "you" span is needed.

decisions.choice: fahari (B); kitu cha kujivunia (R)
decisions.reason: "Kujisifu" (to praise oneself, to boast) keeps the Greek word at Literal, but in everyday Swahili it is a fault. The boast here is not condemned (m2), so Balanced speaks of "fahari" (honourable pride) and Readable of something "cha kujivunia" (to be proud of).

decisions.choice: de quoi se glorifier (L, B); être fier (R); in 6:13-14 se glorifier (L, B), se vanter (R) in 6:13 and être fier (R) in 6:14
decisions.reason: Literal and Balanced use "se glorifier" for this word family throughout, as in Romans. The boast that rests on one’s own tested work is not condemned here (m2), so Readable says "être fier". In 6:13 the boasting is wrong and Readable says "se vanter"; in 6:14 Paul’s boast in the cross is good and Readable says "être fier".

decisions.choice: "자랑" at every level
decisions.reason: As in Romans: "자랑" is the word for this family through the letter (6:13-14). Korean "자랑" can be good pride as well as bragging, so it serves every level here, where the English Balanced and Readable say "pride".

decisions.choice: "짐" for both the burden of verse 2 and the load of verse 5
decisions.reason: The Greek uses two words, a heavy burden others help carry and the load of responsibility each person carries (the meaning decision). Korean "짐" serves both; verse 2 adds "무거운" at Balanced and Readable, and verse 5 says "자기가 져야 할 짐", so the two remain distinct.

decisions.choice: "khoe mình" (L); "tự hào" (B, R) for this word family (also 6:13-14)
decisions.reason: As in the Vietnamese Romans (2:17), Literal keeps one word, "khoe mình", wherever the Greek family appears, so the reader can trace it to 6:13-14. Here it is the honest pride in one's own work (m2), so Balanced and Readable say "tự hào".

decisions.choice: "gánh nặng" (verse 2); "gánh" (L), "gánh riêng" (B, R) (verse 5)
decisions.reason: Paul uses two words: the heavy loads others help with (m1 of 6:2), and the load of responsibility each must carry (m3). Vietnamese "gánh nặng" and "gánh riêng" keep them apart, so the two verses do not seem to contradict each other.

source.text: Κοινωνείτω δὲ ὁ κατηχούμενος τὸν λόγον τῷ κατηχοῦντι ἐν πᾶσιν ἀγαθοῖς.

records.literal_gloss: Let share now the [one] being taught the word with the [one] teaching in all good things.

en.L: Now let the one who is taught the word share in all good things with the one who teaches.
en.B: Those who are being taught the word must share all their good things with the one who teaches them.
en.R: If someone teaches you God's message, share with that teacher all the good things you have.

es.L: Ahora bien, que el que es instruido en la palabra comparta en todas las cosas buenas con el que lo instruye.
es.B: Los que reciben enseñanza en la palabra deben compartir todos sus bienes con quien les enseña.
es.R: Si alguien {{plural_you:les|os}} enseña el mensaje de Dios, {{plural_you:compartan|compartid}} con esa persona todo lo bueno que {{plural_you:tienen|tenéis}}.

sw.L: Basi anayefundishwa neno ashiriki pamoja na anayemfundisha katika vitu vyote vizuri.
sw.B: Wanaofundishwa neno wanapaswa kugawana mema yao yote na yule anayewafundisha.
sw.R: Mtu akiwafundisha ujumbe wa Mungu, mshirikisheni mwalimu huyo vitu vyote vizuri mlivyo navyo.

fr.L: Or, que celui à qui l’on enseigne la parole partage en toutes choses bonnes avec celui qui l’enseigne.
fr.B: Ceux à qui l’on enseigne la parole doivent partager avec celui qui les enseigne tout ce qu’ils ont de bon.
fr.R: Si quelqu’un vous enseigne le message de Dieu, partagez avec lui tout ce que vous avez de bon.

ko.L: 말씀을 배우는 사람은 가르치는 사람과 모든 좋은 것을 함께 나누십시오.
ko.B: 말씀을 배우는 사람은 자기를 가르치는 사람과 자기가 가진 모든 좋은 것을 함께 나누어야 합니다.
ko.R: 누가 여러분에게 하나님의 말씀을 가르쳐 준다면, 여러분이 가진 모든 좋은 것을 그 선생님과 함께 나누십시오.

vi.L: Người được dạy lời [của Đức Chúa Trời] hãy chia sẻ mọi điều tốt lành với người dạy mình.
vi.B: Những người được dạy lời Đức Chúa Trời phải chia sẻ mọi điều tốt lành mình có với người dạy mình.
vi.R: Nếu có người dạy anh chị em sứ điệp của Đức Chúa Trời, hãy chia sẻ với người ấy mọi điều tốt đẹp anh chị em có.

decisions.choice: the one taught and the one teaching: a learner and a teacher of the Christian message
decisions.reason: κατηχέω is the word for instruction by word of mouth. λόγον is "the word", the message of the gospel, so this is about those who teach the faith in the church.

decisions.choice: share all good things: support the teacher, especially with material help
alternatives: the teacher and the taught share all good things together
decisions.reason: κοινωνέω means to have a share, a partnership. Paul elsewhere argues that those who teach the gospel should be supported by those they teach (1 Corinthians 9:11, 14; Romans 15:27). "All good things" is wider than money, but includes it, and verses 9-10 go on to doing good.

decisions.choice: now: a new instruction, loosely linked to what precedes
decisions.reason: δὲ can mark contrast: each carries his or her own load, but the learner should share with the teacher. It more likely marks a new point in a list of practical instructions.

decisions.choice: God's message
decisions.reason: Readable says whose word is being taught (m1).

decisions.choice: "lời [của Đức Chúa Trời]" (L)
decisions.reason: The word is the Christian message (m1). Vietnamese "lời" alone would be any word, so Literal brackets whose word it is; Balanced says it plainly.

source.text: μὴ πλανᾶσθε, θεὸς οὐ μυκτηρίζεται· ὃ γὰρ ἐὰν σπείρῃ ἄνθρωπος, τοῦτο καὶ θερίσει·

records.literal_gloss: Not be misled, God not is mocked; for whatever if sows a man, this also he will reap;

en.L: Do not be led astray; God is not mocked. For whatever {{gender:a person|a man}} sows, that {{gender:they|he}} will also reap.
en.B: Do not let anyone mislead you: God is not to be sneered at. Whatever people sow, that is what they will reap.
en.R: Do not fool yourselves. No one can sneer at God and get away with it. People will harvest whatever they plant.

es.L: No {{plural_you:sean|seáis}} extraviados: Dios no es objeto de burla. Porque cualquier cosa que siembre una persona, eso mismo cosechará también.
es.B: No {{plural_you:permitan|permitáis}} que nadie {{plural_you:los|os}} engañe: Dios no es alguien de quien uno pueda mofarse. Lo que la gente siembre, eso cosechará.
es.R: No {{plural_you:se engañen|os engañéis}} a {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} mismos. Nadie puede burlarse de Dios y salir bien parado. Cada persona cosechará lo que haya sembrado.

sw.L: Msipotoshwe; Mungu hafanyiwi dharau; kwa maana lolote atakalopanda mtu, hilo pia atalivuna.
sw.B: Mtu yeyote asiwapotoshe: Mungu si wa kudharauliwa. Watu watavuna kile kile wanachopanda.
sw.R: Msijidanganye. Hakuna anayeweza kumdharau Mungu na kuepuka matokeo yake. Watu watavuna chochote wanachopanda.

fr.L: Ne vous laissez pas égarer : Dieu ne se laisse pas narguer. Car ce que sème un {{gender:être humain|homme}}, cela aussi il le moissonnera.
fr.B: Ne vous laissez pas tromper : on ne nargue pas Dieu. Ce que chacun sème, c’est cela qu’il récoltera.
fr.R: Ne vous faites pas d’illusions. Personne ne peut se moquer de Dieu sans en subir les conséquences. Chacun récoltera ce qu’il a planté.

ko.L: 속지 마십시오. 하나님은 업신여김을 받지 않으십니다. 사람이 무엇을 심든지 그것을 또한 거둘 것입니다.
ko.B: 아무에게도 속지 마십시오. 하나님은 비웃음을 당하실 분이 아닙니다. 사람은 무엇을 심든지 그것을 거둘 것입니다.
ko.R: 스스로 속지 마십시오. 하나님을 비웃고도 무사할 사람은 아무도 없습니다. 사람은 자기가 심은 것을 그대로 거둘 것입니다.

vi.L: Đừng để bị lừa dối; Đức Chúa Trời không chịu để người ta khinh nhạo đâu. Vì người nào gieo gì thì sẽ gặt nấy.
vi.B: Đừng để ai lừa dối anh chị em: Đức Chúa Trời không để cho ai khinh nhờn {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}. Ai gieo gì thì sẽ gặt nấy.
vi.R: Đừng tự lừa dối mình. Không ai có thể khinh thường Đức Chúa Trời mà tránh được hậu quả. Người ta trồng gì thì sẽ gặt nấy.

decisions.choice: do not be misled: do not deceive yourselves or let others deceive you
decisions.reason: πλανᾶσθε can be passive ("do not be led astray") or middle ("do not deceive yourselves"). Both fit: Paul has warned of self-deception in verse 3 and of the people misleading them throughout the letter (1:7; 5:10).

decisions.choice: God is not sneered at: no one treats God with contempt and escapes the outcome
decisions.reason: μυκτηρίζω means to turn up one's nose, to sneer at. People may live as though God's warnings do not matter, but they will not get away with it. The saying that follows explains why.

decisions.choice: sowing and reaping: what a person does decides what follows from it
decisions.reason: The farming picture was a common proverb (Job 4:8; Proverbs 22:8; Hosea 8:7; 2 Corinthians 9:6). Verse 8 applies it: what is sown into the flesh and what is sown into the Spirit bring two different harvests.

decisions.choice: {{gender:a person|a man}} ... {{gender:they|he}}
decisions.reason: The proverb is about anyone; Literal keeps the singular with the gender setting, and Balanced and Readable make it plural.

decisions.choice: No one can sneer at God and get away with it
decisions.reason: Readable says what the short saying means (m2).

decisions.choice: plant, harvest
decisions.reason: "Sow" and "reap" are less common words for younger readers; Readable uses plain farming words and keeps the picture.

decisions.choice: sembrar, cosechar
decisions.reason: The English Readable changes "sow" and "reap" to plainer words. In Spanish "sembrar" and "cosechar" are themselves the everyday farming words, so Readable keeps them, here and in verses 8-9.

decisions.choice: un {{gender:être humain|homme}} (L); chacun (B, R), with no span
decisions.reason: The proverb is about anyone. Literal keeps the noun and carries the setting on it; the "il" that follows refers to both options and needs none. Balanced and Readable say "chacun", already inclusive.

decisions.choice: narguer (L, B)
decisions.reason: The verb means to turn up one's nose, to sneer at (m2); "narguer" keeps that contempt.

decisions.choice: "khinh nhạo" (L); "khinh nhờn" (B)
decisions.reason: The verb is to sneer at, treat with contempt (m2). "Khinh nhờn" is the Vietnamese for treating what is holy with contempt; "chế nhạo" is only mockery.

source.text: ὅτι ὁ σπείρων εἰς τὴν σάρκα ἑαυτοῦ ἐκ τῆς σαρκὸς θερίσει φθοράν, ὁ δὲ σπείρων εἰς τὸ πνεῦμα ἐκ τοῦ πνεύματος θερίσει ζωὴν αἰώνιον.

records.literal_gloss: For the [one] sowing to the flesh of himself, from the flesh will reap decay, but the [one] sowing to the Spirit, from the Spirit will reap life eternal.

en.L: For the one who sows to {{gender:their|his}} own flesh will reap decay from the flesh, but the one who sows to the Spirit will reap eternal life from the Spirit.
en.B: Those who sow into their own flesh will gather a harvest of decay from the flesh; those who sow into the Spirit will gather from the Spirit a harvest of eternal life.
en.R: If you plant to satisfy your own sinful desires, the harvest they give you will be ruin. But if you plant what the Spirit wants, the Spirit will give you a harvest of eternal life.

es.L: Porque quien siembra en su propia carne cosechará de la carne corrupción; pero quien siembra en el Espíritu cosechará del Espíritu vida eterna.
es.B: Los que siembran en el campo de su propia carne recogerán de la carne una cosecha de corrupción; los que siembran en el campo del Espíritu recogerán del Espíritu una cosecha de vida eterna.
es.R: Si {{plural_you:siembran|sembráis}} para darle a {{plural_you:su|vuestro}} yo pecador lo que quiere, lo que {{plural_you:cosecharán|cosecharéis}} será la ruina. Pero si {{plural_you:siembran|sembráis}} lo que el Espíritu quiere, el Espíritu {{plural_you:les|os}} dará una cosecha de vida eterna.

sw.L: Kwa sababu anayepanda katika mwili wake mwenyewe atavuna uozo kutokana na mwili, bali anayepanda katika Roho atavuna uzima wa milele kutokana na Roho.
sw.B: Wanaopanda katika asili yao ya dhambi watavuna uozo kutoka kwayo; lakini wanaopanda katika Roho watavuna kutoka kwa Roho mavuno ya uzima wa milele.
sw.R: Mkipanda ili kuipa asili yenu ya dhambi kile inachotaka, mavuno mtakayopata ni maangamizi. Lakini mkipanda yale ambayo Roho anataka, Roho atawapa mavuno ya uzima wa milele.

fr.L: Car celui qui sème pour sa propre chair moissonnera de la chair la corruption, mais celui qui sème pour l’Esprit moissonnera de l’Esprit la vie éternelle.
fr.B: Celui qui sème dans sa propre chair récoltera de la chair une moisson de corruption ; celui qui sème dans l’Esprit récoltera de l’Esprit une moisson de vie éternelle.
fr.R: Si vous plantez pour satisfaire votre nature pécheresse, la récolte qu’elle vous donnera sera la ruine. Mais si vous plantez ce que l’Esprit veut, l’Esprit vous donnera une récolte de vie éternelle.

ko.L: 자기 육신에 심는 사람은 육신에서 썩어짐을 거두고, 성령에 심는 사람은 성령에게서 영원한 생명을 거둘 것입니다.
ko.B: 자기 육신을 위해 심는 사람은 육신에게서 썩어 없어질 것을 거두고, 성령을 위해 심는 사람은 성령께서 주시는 영원한 생명을 거둘 것입니다.
ko.R: 자기 안의 죄에 끌리는 본성을 만족시키려고 심는 사람은 멸망을 거둘 것입니다. 그러나 성령께서 원하시는 것을 심는 사람은 성령께서 주시는 영원한 생명을 거둘 것입니다.

vi.L: Vì người gieo cho xác thịt của mình sẽ từ xác thịt mà gặt sự hư nát, nhưng người gieo cho Thánh Linh sẽ từ Thánh Linh mà gặt sự sống đời đời.
vi.B: Người gieo vào xác thịt của mình sẽ gặt từ xác thịt một mùa hư nát; còn người gieo vào Thánh Linh sẽ gặt từ Thánh Linh một mùa sự sống đời đời.
vi.R: Nếu anh chị em gieo để thỏa mãn những ham muốn tội lỗi của mình, thì mùa gặt anh chị em nhận được sẽ là sự hư hoại. Nhưng nếu anh chị em gieo những gì Thánh Linh muốn, thì Thánh Linh sẽ ban cho anh chị em một mùa gặt là sự sống đời đời.

decisions.choice: flesh: the sinful human self that opposes the Spirit, as in 5:13-24
alternatives: reliance on circumcision and the law
decisions.reason: σάρκα is set against πνεῦμα, as flesh and Spirit are set against each other in 5:16-17. Sowing to one's flesh is living for the desires listed in 5:19-21. Some hear an allusion to circumcision too, since verses 12-13 speak of boasting in the flesh, but the word "own" points to a person's own sinful self.

decisions.choice: decay: corruption that ends in ruin and death
decisions.reason: φθοράν is the decay of what perishes (Romans 8:21; 1 Corinthians 15:42). It stands opposite eternal life: the harvest of the flesh rots away, while the Spirit's harvest lasts.

decisions.choice: the Spirit: God's Holy Spirit
decisions.reason: Unlike the flesh, the Spirit is not called the person's "own". It is the Spirit of 5:16-25, who gives life (5:25) and whose fruit is listed in 5:22-23.

decisions.choice: gather a harvest (B); harvest (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable spell out the farming picture so that the two harvests stand side by side.

decisions.choice: your own sinful desires
decisions.reason: Readable says what "flesh" means here (m1), as in chapter 5.

decisions.choice: if you plant
decisions.reason: Readable addresses the reader directly to keep the sentence short.

decisions.choice: carne (L, B); yo pecador (R)
decisions.reason: Follows the choice recorded at 5:13 for the flesh and Spirit passage: here "flesh" is the sinful human self opposed to the Spirit (m1), and Literal and Balanced keep the familiar "carne" while Readable says "yo pecador" (sinful self). In verses 12-13 "flesh" is the body that bears circumcision, so "carne" stays there too.

decisions.choice: mwili (L); asili ya dhambi (B, R)
decisions.reason: Follows the choice recorded at 5:13 for the flesh and Spirit passage: here the word means the sinful self opposed to the Spirit (m1), so Balanced and Readable say "asili ya dhambi" (sinful nature) and Literal keeps "mwili". In verses 12-13 the word is the body that bears circumcision, so "mwili" stays there at every level.

decisions.choice: "영원한 생명" at every level
decisions.reason: The style guide gives "영원한 생명" for eternal life at every level; "영생" is the familiar contraction.

decisions.choice: "sự sống đời đời" at every level
decisions.reason: The style guide's form for eternal life, as in the Vietnamese John and Romans.

source.text: τὸ δὲ καλὸν ποιοῦντες μὴ ἐγκακῶμεν, καιρῷ γὰρ ἰδίῳ θερίσομεν μὴ ἐκλυόμενοι.

records.literal_gloss: And the good doing not let us grow weary, for in time own we will reap, not giving up.

en.L: And let us not lose heart in doing what is good, for in [its] own time we will reap, if we do not grow slack.
en.B: We must not tire of doing good. When the right time comes we will bring in the harvest, as long as we do not slacken.
en.R: So let us not get tired of doing good things. If we keep going and do not quit, we will have a harvest when the time is right.

es.L: Y haciendo lo bueno, no desfallezcamos, porque en [su] propio tiempo cosecharemos, si no aflojamos.
es.B: No debemos cansarnos de obrar el bien. Cuando llegue el momento oportuno, recogeremos la cosecha, siempre que no aflojemos.
es.R: Así que sigamos haciendo el bien sin cansarnos. Si no nos rendimos, tendremos una cosecha cuando llegue el momento.

sw.L: Na katika kufanya yaliyo mazuri tusikate tamaa, kwa maana kwa majira [yake] yenyewe tutavuna, tusipolegea.
sw.B: Hatupaswi kuchoka kufanya mema. Wakati unaofaa ukifika tutavuna mavuno, ikiwa hatutalegea.
sw.R: Kwa hiyo tusichoshwe na kutenda mambo mema. Tukiendelea bila kukata tamaa, tutapata mavuno wakati ufaao.

fr.L: Et en faisant le bien, ne perdons pas courage, car au temps voulu nous moissonnerons, si nous ne faiblissons pas.
fr.B: Ne nous décourageons pas de faire le bien. Le moment venu, nous récolterons, si nous ne baissons pas les bras.
fr.R: Alors ne nous fatiguons pas de faire le bien. Si nous continuons sans abandonner, nous aurons une récolte au bon moment.

ko.L: 우리가 선을 행하다가 낙심하지 맙시다. 포기하지 않으면 때가 이르러 거두게 될 것입니다.
ko.B: 선한 일을 하다가 지치지 맙시다. 우리가 포기하지 않으면, 때가 되어 거두게 될 것입니다.
ko.R: 그러므로 좋은 일을 하는 데 지치지 맙시다. 우리가 그만두지 않고 계속하면, 알맞은 때에 거두게 될 것입니다.

vi.L: Chúng ta đừng mỏi mệt trong việc làm điều lành, vì đến đúng kỳ chúng ta sẽ gặt, nếu chúng ta không bỏ cuộc.
vi.B: Chúng ta đừng chán nản trong việc làm điều tốt. Khi đến đúng thời điểm, chúng ta sẽ gặt hái, miễn là chúng ta không buông xuôi.
vi.R: Vậy chúng ta đừng mệt mỏi trong việc làm điều tốt. Nếu chúng ta cứ tiếp tục và không bỏ cuộc, chúng ta sẽ có mùa gặt khi đến đúng lúc.

decisions.choice: in its own time: the time God has set, the final harvest
alternatives: sooner or later in this life
decisions.reason: καιρῷ ἰδίῳ is "the proper time", the time that belongs to the harvest. After the eternal life of verse 8, it most naturally means the day God has fixed for gathering the harvest, though good may also come of good deeds sooner.

decisions.choice: if we do not give up: a condition for reaping
alternatives: describing the harvest: we will reap without growing weary
decisions.reason: The participle ἐκλυόμενοι most likely states a condition: the harvest comes to those who do not slacken. It repeats the warning of the first clause.

decisions.choice: If we keep going and do not quit, we will have a harvest
alternatives: we will reap, if we do not give up
decisions.reason: Readable puts the condition first, which is easier to follow.

source.text: ἄρα οὖν ὡς καιρὸν ἔχομεν, ἐργαζώμεθα τὸ ἀγαθὸν πρὸς πάντας, μάλιστα δὲ πρὸς τοὺς οἰκείους τῆς πίστεως.

records.literal_gloss: So then as opportunity we have, let us work the good toward all, especially now toward the members of the household of the faith.

en.L: So then, while we have opportunity, let us work what is good toward all [people], and especially toward those of the household of the faith.
en.B: So whenever we have the chance, we should do good to everyone, and above all to those who belong to the family of faith.
en.R: So whenever we have the chance, let us do good to everyone, and most of all to our fellow believers, the family that shares our faith.

es.L: Así pues, mientras tenemos ocasión, practiquemos el bien para con todos, y sobre todo para con los miembros de la casa de la fe.
es.B: Así que, cada vez que se nos presente la ocasión, hagamos el bien a todos, y ante todo a quienes pertenecen a la familia de la fe.
es.R: Por eso, cada vez que podamos, hagamos el bien a todos, y sobre todo a los demás creyentes, la familia que comparte nuestra fe.

sw.L: Kwa hiyo basi, maadamu tuna nafasi, tutende lililo jema kwa wote, na hasa kwa wale wa nyumba ya imani.
sw.B: Kwa hiyo, kila tunapopata fursa, tuwatendee wote mema, na zaidi ya yote wale walio wa familia ya imani.
sw.R: Kwa hiyo, kila tunapopata nafasi, tuwatendee watu wote mema, hasa waumini wenzetu, walio familia moja nasi katika imani.

fr.L: Ainsi donc, tandis que nous en avons l’occasion, pratiquons le bien envers tous, et surtout envers ceux de la maison de la foi.
fr.B: Alors, chaque fois que nous en avons l’occasion, faisons du bien à tous, et surtout à ceux qui font partie de la famille de la foi.
fr.R: Alors, chaque fois que nous le pouvons, faisons du bien à tout le monde, et surtout aux autres croyants, la famille qui partage notre foi.

ko.L: 그러므로 우리에게 기회가 있는 동안, 모든 [사람]에게 선을 행하되, 특히 믿음의 가족에게 [그리합시다].
ko.B: 그러므로 기회가 있을 때마다 모든 사람에게 선을 행합시다. 특히 믿음의 가족에게 그렇게 합시다.
ko.R: 그러므로 기회가 있을 때마다 모든 사람에게 좋은 일을 합시다. 특히 함께 믿는 사람들, 곧 같은 믿음을 가진 가족에게 더욱 그렇게 합시다.

vi.L: Vậy, khi còn có cơ hội, chúng ta hãy làm điều lành cho mọi người, nhất là cho những người thuộc gia đình của đức tin.
vi.B: Vậy, bất cứ khi nào có dịp, chúng ta hãy làm điều tốt cho mọi người, và nhất là cho những người thuộc về gia đình đức tin.
vi.R: Vậy, bất cứ khi nào có dịp, chúng ta hãy làm điều tốt cho mọi người, và nhất là cho các tín hữu, là gia đình cùng chung đức tin với chúng ta.

decisions.choice: as we have opportunity: whenever, and while, the time is ours
decisions.reason: ὡς with καιρὸν can mean "whenever" or "while". καιρός is the same word as "time" in verse 9: the harvest has its time, and the present is the time for sowing. Both senses are present: every chance that comes, while it lasts.

decisions.choice: the household of the faith: fellow believers, God's family
decisions.reason: οἰκείους means members of a household. Paul pictures believers as one family (compare Ephesians 2:19), bound together by the faith they share. They have a first claim, but not the only claim, on one another's help.

decisions.choice: family
decisions.reason: "Household" is now a formal word; "family" keeps the picture. Literal keeps "household".

decisions.choice: our fellow believers, the family that shares our faith
decisions.reason: Readable names the people meant and keeps the key word "faith".

decisions.choice: "gia đình của đức tin" (L), "gia đình đức tin" (B); "các tín hữu" (R)
decisions.reason: The household is God's family of fellow believers (m2). "Gia đình" says the family bond in current Vietnamese; "nhà" alone would be heard as the building.

source.text: Ἴδετε πηλίκοις ὑμῖν γράμμασιν ἔγραψα τῇ ἐμῇ χειρί.

records.literal_gloss: See with how large to you letters I wrote with the my hand.

en.L: See with what large letters I have written to you with my own hand.
en.B: Notice what large letters I make as I write to you in my own hand.
en.R: Now I am writing to you myself, in my own handwriting. Look how big the letters are!

es.L: {{plural_you:Miren|Mirad}} con qué letras tan grandes {{plural_you:les|os}} he escrito con mi propia mano.
es.B: {{plural_you:Fíjense|Fijaos}} en las letras tan grandes que hago al {{plural_you:escribirles|escribiros}} de mi propia mano.
es.R: Ahora {{plural_you:les|os}} escribo yo mismo, con mi propia letra. ¡{{plural_you:Miren|Mirad}} qué grandes son las letras!

sw.L: Oneni ni herufi kubwa kiasi gani ambazo nimewaandikia kwa mkono wangu.
sw.B: Angalieni herufi kubwa ninazoandika ninapowaandikia kwa mkono wangu mimi mwenyewe.
sw.R: Sasa ninawaandikia mimi mwenyewe, kwa mwandiko wangu. Tazameni jinsi herufi zilivyo kubwa!

fr.L: Voyez avec quelles grandes lettres je vous ai écrit de ma propre main.
fr.B: Voyez avec quelles grandes lettres je vous écris de ma propre main.
fr.R: Maintenant, je vous écris moi-même, de ma propre main. Regardez comme les lettres sont grandes !

ko.L: 보십시오, 내가 내 손으로 여러분에게 이렇게 큰 글자로 썼습니다.
ko.B: 내가 내 손으로 직접 여러분에게 쓰는 이 글자가 얼마나 큰지 보십시오.
ko.R: 이제 나는 여러분에게 내 손으로 직접 씁니다. 글씨가 얼마나 큰지 보십시오!

vi.L: Hãy xem tôi viết cho anh chị em bằng những chữ lớn thế nào, bằng chính tay tôi.
vi.B: Hãy để ý xem tôi viết những chữ to thế nào khi tự tay viết cho anh chị em.
vi.R: Bây giờ chính tôi đang viết cho anh chị em, bằng chữ viết tay của tôi. Hãy xem các chữ to biết bao!

decisions.choice: Paul takes the pen from his scribe to write the end of the letter himself
alternatives: Paul wrote the whole letter by hand
decisions.reason: Letters were usually dictated to a scribe (Romans 16:22), and the sender often added the last lines himself to show that the letter was genuine (1 Corinthians 16:21; Colossians 4:18; 2 Thessalonians 3:17). It is likely that this is the point where Paul's own hand begins.

decisions.choice: I have written: a letter-writer's past tense, meaning "I am writing"
alternatives: looking back over the whole letter
decisions.reason: Writers of letters often used the past tense ἔγραψα from the point of view of the reader, for whom the writing is past when the letter arrives. Here it most likely refers to these closing lines.

decisions.choice: large letters: written large for emphasis
alternatives: large because Paul could not see well (compare 4:15)
large because he was not a trained scribe
decisions.reason: πηλίκοις is "how large", not "how long": Paul is speaking of the size of the letters, not the length of the letter. Large writing draws the eye, as underlining does, to the summary that follows. Other reasons have been suggested, such as poor eyesight; the text does not say.

decisions.choice: Now I am writing to you myself, in my own handwriting. Look how big the letters are!
decisions.reason: Readable explains the change of hand (m1, m2) before the call to look.

decisions.choice: je vous écris (B, R); je vous ai écrit (L)
decisions.reason: The past tense is the letter-writer's, seen from the reader's side (m2). French, like English, says it in the present; Literal keeps the past.

source.text: ὅσοι θέλουσιν εὐπροσωπῆσαι ἐν σαρκί, οὗτοι ἀναγκάζουσιν ὑμᾶς περιτέμνεσθαι, μόνον ἵνα τῷ σταυρῷ τοῦ Χριστοῦ μὴ διώκωνται·

records.literal_gloss: As many as want to make a good showing in flesh, these compel you to be circumcised, only so that for the cross of the Christ they may not be persecuted;

en.L: As many as want to make a good showing in [the] flesh, these are trying to compel you to be circumcised, only so that they may not be persecuted for the cross of the {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}.
en.B: The people who want to make a fine impression in the flesh are the ones pressing you to be circumcised. They have one motive: they do not want to suffer persecution because of the cross of {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}.
en.R: Some people want to look good because of what has been done to their bodies. They are the ones trying to force you to be circumcised. They have only one reason: they do not want to be persecuted for holding to the message of the cross of {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}.

es.L: Cuantos quieren dar buena apariencia en [la] carne, estos tratan de obligar{{plural_you:los|os}} a circuncidar{{plural_you:se|os}}, solo para no ser perseguidos por la cruz del {{christos:Cristo|Mesías}}.
es.B: Los que quieren quedar bien en la carne son los que {{plural_you:los|os}} presionan para que {{plural_you:se circunciden|os circuncidéis}}. Tienen un solo motivo: no quieren sufrir persecución por causa de la cruz {{christos:de Cristo|del Mesías}}.
es.R: Hay quienes quieren quedar bien por lo que se ha hecho en su cuerpo. Son ellos los que tratan de obligar{{plural_you:los|os}} a circuncidar{{plural_you:se|os}}. Lo hacen por una sola razón: no quieren ser perseguidos por aferrarse al mensaje de la cruz {{christos:de Cristo|del Mesías}}.

sw.L: Wote wanaotaka kuonekana vizuri katika mwili, hao wanajaribu kuwalazimisha mtahiriwe, ili tu wasiteswe kwa sababu ya msalaba wa {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}}.
sw.B: Watu wanaotaka kujionyesha wazuri katika mwili ndio wanaowasukuma mtahiriwe. Wana lengo moja tu: hawataki kuteswa kwa sababu ya msalaba wa {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}}.
sw.R: Watu fulani wanataka kuonekana wazuri kwa sababu ya kile kilichofanywa kwenye miili yao. Hao ndio wanaojaribu kuwalazimisha mtahiriwe. Wana sababu moja tu: hawataki kuteswa kwa kushikilia ujumbe wa msalaba wa {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}}.

fr.L: Tous ceux qui veulent faire bonne figure dans la chair, ceux-là cherchent à vous contraindre à vous faire circoncire, seulement pour ne pas être persécutés à cause de la croix du {{christos:Christ|Messie}}.
fr.B: Ceux qui veulent se faire bien voir dans la chair, ce sont eux qui vous poussent à vous faire circoncire. Ils n’ont qu’un seul motif : ne pas être persécutés à cause de la croix du {{christos:Christ|Messie}}.
fr.R: Il y a des gens qui veulent paraître respectables grâce à ce qui a été fait à leur corps. Ce sont eux qui essaient de vous obliger à vous faire circoncire. Ils n’ont qu’une seule raison : ils ne veulent pas être persécutés pour être restés attachés au message de la croix du {{christos:Christ|Messie}}.

ko.L: 육신으로 좋은 모양을 내려는 사람들, 바로 이들이 여러분에게 할례를 받으라고 강요하고 있습니다. 다만 {{christos:그리스도|메시아}}의 십자가 때문에 박해를 받지 않으려는 것입니다.
ko.B: 육신으로 좋은 인상을 주려는 사람들이 여러분에게 할례를 받으라고 강요합니다. 그들의 속셈은 오직 하나, {{christos:그리스도|메시아}}의 십자가 때문에 박해를 받지 않으려는 것입니다.
ko.R: 어떤 사람들은 자기 몸에 한 일 때문에 남에게 잘 보이고 싶어 합니다. 그들이 바로 여러분에게 할례를 받으라고 강요하는 사람들입니다. 그들이 그러는 데에는 한 가지 이유밖에 없습니다. {{christos:그리스도|메시아}}의 십자가에 관한 말씀을 붙들었다가 박해를 받고 싶지 않은 것입니다.

vi.L: Tất cả những người muốn được tiếng tốt trong xác thịt, chính họ ép anh chị em chịu cắt bì, chỉ để họ khỏi bị bắt bớ vì thập tự giá của {{christos:Đấng Christ|Đấng Mê-si-a}}.
vi.B: Những người muốn gây ấn tượng tốt về mặt xác thịt chính là những người đang ép anh chị em chịu cắt bì. Họ chỉ có một mục đích: họ không muốn chịu bắt bớ vì thập tự giá của {{christos:Đấng Christ|Đấng Mê-si-a}}.
vi.R: Có một số người muốn được người khác khen vì những gì đã được làm trên thân thể họ. Họ chính là những người đang cố ép anh chị em chịu cắt bì. Họ chỉ có một lý do: họ không muốn bị bắt bớ vì giữ sứ điệp về thập tự giá của {{christos:Đấng Christ|Đấng Mê-si-a}}.

decisions.choice: make a good showing in the flesh: win approval by an outward mark in the body
alternatives: look good by human standards in general
decisions.reason: εὐπροσωπέω means to put on a good face. "In the flesh" here points to circumcision, a mark cut in the body (verse 13), which would make them look respectable to those who prized it.

decisions.choice: are trying to compel: the pressure is real, but the Galatians have not yet given in
decisions.reason: The present ἀναγκάζουσιν describes ongoing pressure. Paul used the same verb of Titus, who was not compelled to be circumcised (2:3), and of Peter compelling Gentiles to live like Jews (2:14).

decisions.choice: persecuted for the cross: opposed by those who saw a gospel without circumcision as abandoning God's law
decisions.reason: Paul says he himself is persecuted because he does not preach circumcision; if he did, "the offense of the cross" would be removed (5:11). A message that Christ crucified is enough, without the law, drew hostility from many of Paul's fellow Jews (1:13; 4:29). The dative σταυρῷ gives the cause.

decisions.choice: these: the teachers troubling the Galatians
decisions.reason: οὗτοι points back to the people who are unsettling the churches (1:7; 5:10, 12). Paul now gives his own judgment on their motives.

decisions.choice: {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} (L); {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} (B, R)
decisions.reason: Title setting. Literal keeps the article.

decisions.choice: for holding to the message of the cross
decisions.reason: Readable says that the persecution is for the message of the cross, not for the wooden cross itself (m3).

decisions.choice: because of what has been done to their bodies
decisions.reason: Readable says what "flesh" refers to here (m1).

decisions.choice: "육신으로" (L, B); "자기 몸에 한 일 때문에" (R), here and in verse 13
decisions.reason: The flesh here is the body that bears the outward mark of circumcision (the meaning decision). Literal and Balanced keep the letter's word; Readable says what it refers to, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: "xác thịt" (L, B); "thân thể" (R) in 6:12-13
decisions.reason: Here flesh is the body that bears the mark of circumcision (m1), not the sinful self of 5:13-24, so Readable says "thân thể", as the English Readable says "bodies"; Literal and Balanced keep "xác thịt", which carries Paul's irony.

source.text: οὐδὲ γὰρ οἱ περιτεμνόμενοι αὐτοὶ νόμον φυλάσσουσιν, ἀλλὰ θέλουσιν ὑμᾶς περιτέμνεσθαι ἵνα ἐν τῇ ὑμετέρᾳ σαρκὶ καυχήσωνται.

records.literal_gloss: For not even those being circumcised themselves law keep, but they want you to be circumcised so that in your flesh they may boast.

en.L: For not even those who are circumcised themselves keep [the] law, but they want you to be circumcised so that they may boast in your flesh.
en.B: For even these circumcised people do not themselves obey the law. What they want is your circumcision, so that your flesh can be something for them to boast about.
en.R: These people are circumcised, but even they do not obey the law. They want you to be circumcised only so they can brag about what was done to your body.

es.L: Porque ni siquiera los que se circuncidan cumplen ellos mismos [la] ley; pero quieren que {{plural_you:sean|seáis}} circuncidados a fin de gloriarse en {{plural_you:su|vuestra}} carne.
es.B: Porque ni siquiera estos circuncidados obedecen ellos mismos la ley. Lo que quieren es que {{plural_you:se circunciden|os circuncidéis}}, para poder jactarse de la carne de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}.
es.R: Esas personas están circuncidadas, pero ni siquiera ellas obedecen la ley. Quieren que {{plural_you:se circunciden|os circuncidéis}} solo para poder presumir de lo que se hizo en el cuerpo de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}.

sw.L: Kwa maana hata wanaotahiriwa wenyewe hawaitunzi sheria, ila wanataka mtahiriwe ili wapate kujisifu juu ya mwili wenu.
sw.B: Hata hao waliotahiriwa hawaitii sheria wenyewe. Wanachotaka ni tohara yenu, ili mwili wenu uwe kitu cha wao kujisifia.
sw.R: Watu hao wametahiriwa, lakini hata wao hawaitii sheria. Wanataka mtahiriwe ili tu wapate kujigamba kwa kile kilichofanywa kwenye miili yenu.

fr.L: Car même ceux qui se font circoncire ne gardent pas eux-mêmes la Loi, mais ils veulent que vous soyez circoncis afin de se glorifier dans votre chair.
fr.B: Car même ces circoncis n’observent pas eux-mêmes la Loi. Ce qu’ils veulent, c’est votre circoncision, pour pouvoir se glorifier de votre chair.
fr.R: Ces gens sont circoncis, mais eux-mêmes n’obéissent pas à la Loi. Ils veulent que vous soyez circoncis uniquement pour pouvoir se vanter de ce qui a été fait à votre corps.

ko.L: 할례를 받는 그들 자신도 율법을 지키지 않으면서, 여러분의 육신을 자랑하려고 여러분이 할례를 받기를 원합니다.
ko.B: 할례를 받은 이 사람들조차 율법을 지키지 않습니다. 그들이 여러분의 할례를 원하는 것은 여러분의 육신을 자기들의 자랑거리로 삼으려는 것입니다.
ko.R: 이 사람들은 할례를 받았지만, 그들조차 율법을 지키지 않습니다. 그들은 여러분의 몸에 한 일을 자랑하려고 여러분에게 할례를 받게 하려는 것뿐입니다.

vi.L: Vì ngay cả những người chịu cắt bì cũng không tự mình giữ luật pháp, nhưng họ muốn anh chị em chịu cắt bì để họ khoe mình về xác thịt của anh chị em.
vi.B: Vì ngay cả những người chịu cắt bì ấy cũng không vâng giữ luật pháp. Họ muốn anh chị em chịu cắt bì là để có cớ khoe khoang về xác thịt của anh chị em.
vi.R: Những người này đã chịu cắt bì, nhưng chính họ cũng không vâng giữ luật pháp. Họ muốn anh chị em chịu cắt bì chỉ để họ có thể khoe khoang về những gì đã được làm trên thân thể anh chị em.

decisions.choice: follow SBLGNT: those who are being circumcised (present)
decisions.reason: Some manuscripts read a perfect participle, "those who have been circumcised". SBLGNT reads περιτεμνόμενοι. Reviewers should check the apparatus.

decisions.choice: those circumcised: the teachers who insist on circumcision
alternatives: Gentile converts who have accepted circumcision
decisions.reason: The present participle could describe Gentiles who are having themselves circumcised, but the sentence goes on "they want you to be circumcised", which fits the teachers of verse 12. The present may describe them as the circumcision party.

decisions.choice: boast in your flesh: take pride in your circumcision as their success
decisions.reason: "Flesh" here is the body that bears circumcision. Paul says the teachers want the Galatians' circumcision as a trophy. Verse 14 sets his own boast, the cross, against it.

decisions.choice: what was done to your body
decisions.reason: Readable says what "flesh" refers to here (m3).

decisions.choice: gloriarse (L); jactarse, presumir (B, R, verse 13); gloriarse, sentirse orgulloso (B, R, verse 14)
decisions.reason: Literal uses "gloriarse" for the one Greek verb in verses 4, 13 and 14, so the reader sees Paul set his boast against the teachers'. Balanced and Readable choose by sense: the teachers' boast is "jactarse" or "presumir", which sound proud, while Paul's boast in the cross is "gloriarse" or "sentirse orgulloso".

decisions.choice: la carne de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}; el cuerpo de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}
decisions.reason: With ustedes, "su carne" could be read as the teachers' own flesh. "La carne de ustedes" makes clear that it is the Galatians' circumcision they want to boast of (m3).

decisions.choice: "khoe khoang" (B, R)
decisions.reason: Here the boasting is pride in one's own success over others (m3), so Balanced and Readable say "khoe khoang", which carries the fault, as the Vietnamese Romans does for the boasting Paul rejects (3:27); Literal keeps "khoe mình".

source.text: ἐμοὶ δὲ μὴ γένοιτο καυχᾶσθαι εἰ μὴ ἐν τῷ σταυρῷ τοῦ κυρίου ἡμῶν Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ, δι’ οὗ ἐμοὶ κόσμος ἐσταύρωται κἀγὼ κόσμῳ.

records.literal_gloss: But to me may it not be to boast except in the cross of the Lord of us Jesus Christ, through which to me [the] world has been crucified and I to [the] world.

en.L: But for me, may it never be [that I] boast except in the cross of our Lord Jesus {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}, through which [the] world has been crucified to me, and I to [the] world.
en.B: But far be it from me to boast of anything except the cross of our Lord Jesus {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}. Through that cross the world has been crucified to me, and I to the world.
en.R: But I will never brag about anything except the cross of our Lord Jesus {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}. Because of that cross, the world and all it prizes is as dead to me as someone nailed to a cross, and I am just as dead to the world.

es.L: Pero en cuanto a mí, nunca me suceda gloriarme sino en la cruz de nuestro Señor {{christos:Jesucristo|Jesús, el Mesías}}, por medio de la cual el mundo ha sido crucificado para mí, y yo para el mundo.
es.B: Pero de ningún modo me gloriaré en otra cosa que no sea la cruz de nuestro Señor {{christos:Jesucristo|Jesús, el Mesías}}. Por medio de esa cruz el mundo ha quedado crucificado para mí, y yo para el mundo.
es.R: Pero yo jamás me sentiré orgulloso de nada, sino de la cruz de nuestro Señor {{christos:Jesucristo|Jesús, el Mesías}}. Por esa cruz, el mundo y todo lo que valora está tan muerto para mí como alguien clavado en una cruz, y yo estoy igual de muerto para el mundo.

sw.L: Lakini kwangu mimi, isiwe kamwe nijisifu isipokuwa katika msalaba wa Bwana wetu Yesu {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}}, ambao kupitia huo ulimwengu umesulubiwa kwangu, na mimi kwa ulimwengu.
sw.B: Lakini mimi sitakubali kamwe kujisifu kwa kitu chochote isipokuwa msalaba wa Bwana wetu Yesu {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}}. Kupitia msalaba huo ulimwengu umesulubiwa kwangu, nami nimesulubiwa kwa ulimwengu.
sw.R: Lakini mimi sitajivunia kitu chochote kamwe isipokuwa msalaba wa Bwana wetu Yesu {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}}. Kwa sababu ya msalaba huo, ulimwengu na yote unayoyathamini ni kama mfu kwangu, kama mtu aliyepigiliwa msalabani, nami nimekuwa mfu kwa ulimwengu vivyo hivyo.

fr.L: Mais pour moi, qu’il n’arrive pas que je me glorifie, si ce n’est dans la croix de notre Seigneur Jésus {{christos:Christ|Messie}}, par laquelle le monde a été crucifié pour moi, et moi pour le monde.
fr.B: Quant à moi, jamais je ne voudrais me glorifier d’autre chose que de la croix de notre Seigneur Jésus {{christos:Christ|le Messie}}. Par cette croix, le monde a été crucifié pour moi, et moi pour le monde.
fr.R: Mais moi, je ne veux être fier de rien, sauf de la croix de notre Seigneur Jésus {{christos:Christ|le Messie}}. À cause de cette croix, le monde et tout ce qu’il admire sont pour moi aussi morts que quelqu’un qu’on a cloué sur une croix, et moi, je suis tout aussi mort pour le monde.

ko.L: 그러나 나에게는 우리 주 예수 {{christos:그리스도|메시아}}의 십자가 외에는 자랑할 것이 결코 없습니다. 그것을 통하여 세상이 나에 대하여 십자가에 못 박혔고, 나도 세상에 대하여 [그러합니다].
ko.B: 그러나 나는 우리 주 예수 {{christos:그리스도|메시아}}의 십자가 말고는 결코 아무것도 자랑하지 않겠습니다. 그 십자가로 말미암아 세상은 나에 대해 십자가에 못 박혔고, 나도 세상에 대해 그렇게 되었습니다.
ko.R: 그러나 나는 우리 주 예수 {{christos:그리스도|메시아}}의 십자가 말고는 아무것도 자랑하지 않을 것입니다. 그 십자가 때문에, 세상과 세상이 귀하게 여기는 모든 것은 십자가에 못 박혀 죽은 사람처럼 나에게 죽은 것이 되었습니다. 그리고 나도 세상에 대해 그렇게 죽은 사람이 되었습니다.

vi.L: Nhưng về phần tôi, không hề có chuyện tôi khoe mình, ngoại trừ về thập tự giá của Chúa chúng ta là Đức Giê-xu {{christos:Christ|Mê-si-a}}, qua đó thế gian đã bị đóng đinh đối với tôi, và tôi đối với thế gian.
vi.B: Nhưng tôi chẳng bao giờ tự hào về điều gì ngoài thập tự giá của Chúa chúng ta là Đức Giê-xu {{christos:Christ|Mê-si-a}}. Qua thập tự giá ấy, thế gian đã bị đóng đinh đối với tôi, và tôi đối với thế gian.
vi.R: Nhưng tôi sẽ không bao giờ tự hào về điều gì, ngoại trừ thập tự giá của Chúa chúng ta là Đức Giê-xu {{christos:Christ|Mê-si-a}}. Nhờ thập tự giá ấy, thế gian và mọi điều thế gian quý trọng đã chết đối với tôi, như người bị đóng đinh trên thập tự giá, và tôi cũng đã chết đối với thế gian như vậy.

decisions.choice: may it never be: the strongest refusal Paul has
decisions.reason: μὴ γένοιτο is the expression Paul uses to reject something outright (2:17; 3:21). Here it is personal: the one thing he will boast in is the cross, in contrast with the teachers who boast in circumcision (verse 13).

decisions.choice: through which: through the cross
decisions.reason: The relative οὗ could refer to the cross or to the Lord Jesus Christ; the form is the same. The sentence is about the cross, and so are verse 12 and 2:19-20, so the cross is the more likely reference. The meaning is much the same either way.

decisions.choice: the world: life organized apart from God, with its standards of status and religious standing
decisions.reason: κόσμος here is "this present evil age" (1:4): its ways of ranking people, including circumcision and the marks of religious status. At the cross that world lost its claim on Paul, and he ceased to count in its eyes.

decisions.choice: crucified to each other: the cross has ended the relationship on both sides
decisions.reason: The perfect ἐσταύρωται speaks of something done and still in effect, as in 2:19, "I have been crucified with Christ". The world is dead to Paul, and Paul is dead to it.

decisions.choice: {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} (L); {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} (B, R)
decisions.reason: Title setting.

decisions.choice: the world and all it prizes is as dead to me as someone nailed to a cross, and I am just as dead to the world
alternatives: the world has been crucified to me, and I to the world
decisions.reason: Readable explains the picture of crucifixion and the sense of "world" (m3, m4).

decisions.choice: far be it from me
decisions.reason: An English expression of strong refusal that does not add God's name.

decisions.choice: nunca me suceda (L); de ningún modo (B)
decisions.reason: Elsewhere μὴ γένοιτο answers a question and is rendered "¡No sea así!" or "¡De ningún modo!". Here it is Paul's own vow (m1), so Literal says "nunca me suceda" and Balanced keeps "de ningún modo" inside the sentence.

decisions.choice: isiwe kamwe (L); sitakubali kamwe (B)
decisions.reason: Elsewhere μὴ γένοιτο answers a question and is rendered "Isiwe hivyo!" or "Hasha!". Here it is Paul's own vow (m1), so Swahili builds it into the sentence: "isiwe kamwe nijisifu" (L), "sitakubali kamwe kujisifu" (B).

decisions.choice: par laquelle (L), the cross
decisions.reason: The Greek relative can point to the cross or to the Lord Jesus Christ (m2), but a French pronoun must agree with one of them. Literal follows the reading m2 prefers, the cross, so it is feminine; Balanced and Readable name the cross.

decisions.choice: "tự hào" (B, R) for boasting in the cross
decisions.reason: The boasting Paul accepts is glad confidence in what God has done (m1), the opposite of the boasting in 6:13, so Balanced and Readable return to "tự hào", as in 6:4 and in the Vietnamese Romans (5:2-11).

decisions.choice: "thế gian" for the world
decisions.reason: The world here is life organized apart from God (m3), "thế gian" as the style guide sets for kosmos; "thế giới" is the physical world.

source.text: οὔτε γὰρ περιτομή τί ἐστιν οὔτε ἀκροβυστία, ἀλλὰ καινὴ κτίσις.

records.literal_gloss: For neither circumcision anything is nor uncircumcision, but a new creation.

en.L: For neither is circumcision anything, nor uncircumcision, but a new creation [is].
en.B: For circumcision is nothing, and uncircumcision is nothing; the one thing that matters is a new creation.
en.R: It does not matter whether a person is circumcised or not. What matters is being part of the new creation God is making.

es.L: Porque ni la circuncisión es algo ni la incircuncisión, sino [que lo es] una creación nueva.
es.B: Porque la circuncisión no es nada, y la incircuncisión tampoco; lo único que importa es una creación nueva.
es.R: No importa si alguien está circuncidado o no. Lo que importa es formar parte de la nueva creación que Dios está haciendo.

sw.L: Kwa maana tohara si kitu chochote, wala kutotahiriwa, ila uumbaji mpya [ndio kitu].
sw.B: Kwa maana tohara si kitu, na kutotahiriwa si kitu; jambo moja lenye maana ni uumbaji mpya.
sw.R: Haijalishi kama mtu ametahiriwa au hajatahiriwa. Kinachojalisha ni kuwa sehemu ya uumbaji mpya ambao Mungu anaufanya.

fr.L: Car ni la circoncision n’est quelque chose, ni l’incirconcision, mais une création nouvelle [l’est].
fr.B: Car la circoncision n’est rien, et l’incirconcision n’est rien : la seule chose qui compte, c’est une création nouvelle.
fr.R: Peu importe qu’on soit circoncis ou non. Ce qui compte, c’est de faire partie de la création nouvelle que Dieu est en train de faire.

ko.L: 할례도 아무것도 아니고 무할례도 [아무것도 아니며], 새로운 창조가 [중요합니다].
ko.B: 할례도 아무것도 아니고, 할례를 받지 않은 것도 아무것도 아닙니다. 중요한 것은 새로운 창조입니다.
ko.R: 사람이 할례를 받았는지 받지 않았는지는 중요하지 않습니다. 중요한 것은 하나님께서 새롭게 만들고 계신 세상에 속하는 것입니다.

vi.L: Vì chịu cắt bì hay không chịu cắt bì chẳng là gì cả, nhưng [điều quan trọng là] một cuộc tạo dựng mới.
vi.B: Vì cắt bì chẳng là gì, mà không cắt bì cũng chẳng là gì; điều duy nhất quan trọng là một cuộc tạo dựng mới.
vi.R: Chịu cắt bì hay không cũng chẳng quan trọng gì. Điều quan trọng là được dự phần vào cuộc tạo dựng mới mà Đức Chúa Trời đang làm.

decisions.choice: follow SBLGNT: "For neither circumcision ..."
alternatives: "For in Christ Jesus neither circumcision avails anything ..."
decisions.reason: Many manuscripts add "in Christ Jesus" and a verb meaning "avails", making the verse match 5:6. The shorter SBLGNT text is better supported by early manuscripts, and copyists tended to make parallel passages agree. Reviewers should check the apparatus.

decisions.choice: a new creation: the new world God has begun in Christ, and each person made new within it
alternatives: only the individual believer made new
only the renewal of the whole world
decisions.reason: καινὴ κτίσις has no article and no "anyone". In 2 Corinthians 5:17 the phrase applies to the person who is in Christ; Isaiah 65:17 speaks of new heavens and a new earth. Here, after "the world has been crucified to me", Paul probably means both: the new age that has begun in Christ, and the person who belongs to it.

decisions.choice: neither circumcision nor uncircumcision counts: being Jew or Gentile gives no standing
decisions.reason: Paul says the same in 5:6 and 1 Corinthians 7:19. Uncircumcision gives no advantage either; the Galatians should not boast of it.

decisions.choice: being part of the new creation God is making
decisions.reason: Readable names God as the one who creates and keeps both the personal and the wider sense (m2).

decisions.choice: uumbaji mpya
decisions.reason: "Kiumbe kipya" (a new creature) names only the person made new. "Uumbaji mpya" (new creation) can hold both senses the meaning decision keeps (m2): the new world God has begun in Christ and each person made new in it.

decisions.choice: "새로운 창조" (L, B); "하나님께서 새롭게 만들고 계신 세상에 속하는 것" (R)
decisions.reason: The meaning decision reads it as the new world God has begun in Christ, and each person made new within it, and marks it uncertain. "새로운 창조" (new creation) keeps both open; "새로운 피조물" (a new creature) would narrow it to the person. Readable says the wider reading, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: "một cuộc tạo dựng mới"
decisions.reason: The meaning decision leaves open whether Paul means the new world God has begun or each person made new in it (m2). "Cuộc tạo dựng mới" names God's new act of creating and can include both, as the Vietnamese Colossians says "cuộc tạo dựng mới" at Readable (1:18); "tạo vật mới" would choose the individual.

source.text: καὶ ὅσοι τῷ κανόνι τούτῳ στοιχήσουσιν, εἰρήνη ἐπ’ αὐτοὺς καὶ ἔλεος, καὶ ἐπὶ τὸν Ἰσραὴλ τοῦ θεοῦ.

records.literal_gloss: And as many as by the rule this will walk, peace upon them and mercy, and upon the Israel of the God.

en.L: And as many as will walk in line with this rule, peace [be] upon them, and mercy, and upon the Israel of God.
en.B: May peace and mercy be on all who live in line with this rule, and on the Israel of God.
en.R: May God give peace and mercy to everyone who lives by this rule, and to the Israel of God.

es.L: Y cuantos caminen en línea con esta regla, paz [sea] sobre ellos, y misericordia, y sobre el Israel de Dios.
es.B: Que la paz y la misericordia estén sobre todos los que vivan según esta regla, y sobre el Israel de Dios.
es.R: Que Dios dé paz y misericordia a todos los que viven según esta regla, y al Israel de Dios.

sw.L: Na wote watakaotembea sambamba na kanuni hii, amani [iwe] kwao, na rehema, na kwa Israeli wa Mungu.
sw.B: Amani na rehema ziwe kwa wote wanaoishi kwa kufuata kanuni hii, na kwa Israeli wa Mungu.
sw.R: Mungu awape amani na rehema wote wanaoishi kwa kanuni hii, na Israeli wa Mungu pia.

fr.L: Et tous ceux qui marcheront en accord avec cette règle, paix sur eux, et miséricorde, ainsi que sur l’Israël de Dieu.
fr.B: Que la paix et la miséricorde soient sur tous ceux qui vivent selon cette règle, et sur l’Israël de Dieu.
fr.R: Que Dieu donne la paix et la miséricorde à tous ceux qui vivent selon cette règle, et à l’Israël de Dieu.

ko.L: 그리고 이 기준을 따라 걷는 사람들에게 평안과 긍휼이 [있기를 빕니다]. 하나님의 이스라엘에게도 [있기를 빕니다].
ko.B: 이 기준을 따라 사는 모든 사람에게, 그리고 하나님의 이스라엘에게 평안과 긍휼이 있기를 빕니다.
ko.R: 이 기준을 따라 사는 모든 사람에게, 그리고 하나님의 이스라엘에게 하나님께서 평안과 긍휼을 베풀어 주시기를 빕니다.

vi.L: Và tất cả những ai sẽ bước theo quy tắc này, nguyện bình an và lòng thương xót ở trên họ, và trên Y-sơ-ra-ên của Đức Chúa Trời.
vi.B: Nguyện bình an và lòng thương xót ở trên tất cả những ai sống theo quy tắc này, và trên Y-sơ-ra-ên của Đức Chúa Trời.
vi.R: Cầu xin Đức Chúa Trời ban bình an và lòng thương xót cho tất cả những ai sống theo quy tắc này, và cho Y-sơ-ra-ên của Đức Chúa Trời.

decisions.choice: walk in line with this rule: live by the standard of verse 15
decisions.reason: κανόνι is a measuring rule, a standard. The rule is what Paul has just said: what counts is not circumcision but a new creation. στοιχέω means to keep in line, as in 5:25, "let us keep in step with the Spirit".

decisions.choice: an echo of the blessing "peace upon Israel"
decisions.reason: Psalms 125:5 and 128:6 end with "peace upon Israel". Paul gives the familiar blessing to those who walk by the rule of the new creation.

decisions.choice: the Israel of God: uncertain whether this is the whole church, Jew and Gentile, or Jewish believers or Israel
alternatives: the whole people of God in Christ, Jewish and Gentile believers together
the people of Israel, for whom Paul prays for mercy
decisions.reason: The phrase occurs only here. If καὶ means "that is", the Israel of God is the same group as those who walk by this rule: all believers, who are Abraham's offspring (3:7, 29). If it means "and also", Paul adds a second group: Jewish believers, or Israel as a people, to whom God will show mercy (Romans 11:26-32). The order "peace ... and mercy" and the strong contrast with the circumcision party are argued on both sides. The grammar allows both.

decisions.choice: May peace and mercy be on ...
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable put the blessing as a prayer, as Paul's greetings are (1:3). Readable names God as the giver.

decisions.choice: "평안과 긍휼" at every level
decisions.reason: "평안" is the key term for peace, as in 1:3; "긍휼" is the established word for God's mercy and is still understood; "자비" is also current but is the Buddhist word for compassion. A reviewer may prefer "자비" for Readable.

vi.B: Từ nay về sau, đừng ai gây phiền nhiễu cho tôi nữa, vì trên thân thể tôi có mang những dấu vết cho thấy tôi thuộc về Đức Giê-xu.
