decisions.choice: from now on
decisions.reason: Τοῦ λοιποῦ is a set phrase for time to come, "henceforth".

decisions.choice: the marks of Jesus: scars from Paul's sufferings for Jesus, which brand him as Jesus' own
alternatives: marks that share in Jesus' wounds in a mystical way
decisions.reason: στίγματα were marks branded or tattooed on slaves, soldiers or devotees of a god to show to whom they belonged. Paul carried scars from beatings and stoning (2 Corinthians 11:23-25; Acts 14:19). Those are his marks: unlike the circumcision the teachers urge, they show he belongs to Jesus, and they are the cost of preaching the cross.

decisions.choice: the marks that show I belong to Jesus (B); The scars on my body show that I belong to Jesus (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what the marks mean (m2); Readable also says what they were.

decisions.choice: les marques (L, B); les cicatrices (R)
decisions.reason: The word was used of the brand that showed whom a slave or devotee belonged to (m2). French "stigmates" comes from it but now suggests the wounds of Christ appearing on a saint's body, which is not Paul's meaning.

decisions.choice: "예수의 흔적" (L); "예수께 속한 사람이라는 표" (B); "상처 자국들" (R)
decisions.reason: The marks are scars from Paul's sufferings, which brand him as Jesus' own (the meaning decision). "흔적" (marks, traces) is plain at Literal; Balanced says what they show, as the English does; "낙인" (brand) would sound like a mark of shame in Korean.

decisions.choice: "dấu vết" (L, B); "vết sẹo" (R)
decisions.reason: The marks are scars from Paul's sufferings, which brand him as Jesus' own (m2). "Dấu vết" is a mark left on the body and keeps the picture of a brand; Readable says "scars".

vi.L: Thưa {{gender:anh chị em|anh em}}, nguyện ân điển của Chúa chúng ta là Đức Giê-xu {{christos:Christ|Mê-si-a}} ở với tâm linh anh chị em. A-men.
vi.B: Thưa {{gender:anh chị em|anh em}}, nguyện ân điển của Chúa chúng ta là Đức Giê-xu {{christos:Christ|Mê-si-a}} ở cùng tâm linh anh chị em. A-men.
vi.R: Thưa {{gender:anh chị em|anh em}}, cầu xin ân điển của Chúa chúng ta là Đức Giê-xu {{christos:Christ|Mê-si-a}} ở cùng mỗi người trong anh chị em. A-men.

decisions.choice: with your spirit: with you yourselves
alternatives: with the human spirit as distinct from the body
decisions.reason: "With your spirit" is a way of saying "with you", as in Philippians 4:23 and Philemon 25; πνεύματος here is the inner person, the whole of who they are.

decisions.choice: brothers: the last word before "amen", a warm address after a severe letter
decisions.reason: This is the only one of Paul's letters to end with ἀδελφοί. After the sharp words of the letter, he closes by calling the Galatians his family. The term includes all the believers, women and men.

decisions.choice: {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}; {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}; {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}
decisions.reason: Title setting and gender setting.

decisions.choice: {{gender:Brothers and sisters|Brothers}} first
alternatives: at the end, as in the Greek
decisions.reason: In English a direct address before "Amen" is awkward; Balanced and Readable place it first.

decisions.choice: with each one of you
decisions.reason: Readable says what the idiom means (m1).

decisions.choice: "{{gender:형제자매|형제}} 여러분" placed first (L)
alternatives: the address at the end, before "아멘"
decisions.reason: Korean puts an address at the start of what is said, and a blessing ending in "빕니다" cannot be followed by the address without breaking the sentence. The warmth the meaning decision notes stays in the address itself.

decisions.choice: the address "Thưa anh chị em" first (L)
alternatives: the address at the end, as in the Greek
decisions.reason: Vietnamese puts the respectful address at the head of the sentence; at the end, after "anh chị em" (you), it would read as the same word twice.

decisions.choice: "tâm linh anh chị em" (L, B)
decisions.reason: "With your spirit" means with you yourselves (m1). "Tâm linh", lowercase, is the human spirit, as in the Vietnamese Colossians (2:5); Readable says "each one of you", as the English Readable does.
